rows.what the ink shows: The symbol has a long left downstroke, a rising shoulder and a descending right return before the subscript bars. It has no central loop like the nearby phi.
A long left stem rises into a pointed shoulder with a short right return, separate from the following subscript bar. The shape repeats the preceding mu.
The subscript has an A, then a raised compact star, then a second A. The star is visibly between the A forms, not after the second.
Above the deletion line, the symbol has a vertical left descender joined diagonally to an upper shoulder and short right stroke. The following two A forms belong to its subscript.
The right-hand symbol has a slanted left descender and rising shoulder ending in a short downward stroke. It is separate from the following A-star-A subscript.

Below the cancellation stroke, the first word retains the descending p and a low connected ar trace. The next word begins with a small curled s and ends in the upright t stroke and low e return; its middle is compressed.

The initial p retains a descender below the lower cancellation line and a small upper bowl. The remaining letter bodies merge into the two heavy horizontal deletion strokes, so rouver cannot be separated securely.
The inserted symbol above the deletion has a long left downstroke, an oblique rise and short upper-right return. The AA-star subscript follows to its right.
The symbol to the right of the crossed-out patch has the same slanted stem and pointed shoulder, with a short terminal downstroke. A-star-A follows below and to the right.

The insertion begins with a small a body and detached accent; support includes two descending p strokes in the compressed connected trace. Compact has a separate initial c, a medial p downstroke and a raised hooked terminal t.
The symbol has a descending left stem, a short return arch and a rightward shoulder; it has no closed upper loop like the nearby phi.
A straight descending stroke rises into a small arch and turns right, repeating the mu form on the left of this equality.
The initial d has an ascending kink; the following reduced letters carry the two e accents and the i dot, ending in a low curved s.

The first word has a looped initial, an i dot and a long terminal t crossbar; the next has a tall crossed t, and the last has a tall l and dotted i. These strokes support doivent être utilis-, but the compressed ending does not separate és from ées.

Initial m humps and an e loop survive, followed by a long strike through the middle and a terminal crossed rise; the next word begins with a tall loop. The strike and reinforcing strokes conceal enough of both words that the full proposed phrase remains uncertain.
Below the diagonal strike, une retains its rounded u and n humps; the second word shows the m humps and connected shallow loops of mesure.
An open initial c hook joins a dark o, followed after a pen lift by the paired m humps and a trailing e stroke. The tall initial hook resembles the C of Compléments on this page.
The title begins with a tall open C, followed by a deeply descending p, a rising l and an acute accent; the compressed ending finishes in a crossed t and s stroke.
The first word retains a deep p stem, a lower o bowl and a low connected ending consistent with pour. The next word has a t-like rise but its remaining letters merge with the heavy crossing-out.
Under the cancellation strokes a tall l remains at the left, a compact o in the middle, and a rounded g with a long descending hook at the right. The g descender is distinct from the added exp above.

After the visible Dans, a continuous cancellation stroke covers the small letter bodies; only isolated lower ticks and a tall terminal stroke survive. They do not securely distinguish the proposed three-word sequence.
The word before the comma begins with a tall t stroke and a small lower loop. The following low bodies run into the cancellation line, so ermes cannot be read separately.

A short lower equality stroke, the following triangular Delta, and parentheses remain visible beneath the crossing line. The tightly overdrawn interior around A does not let me securely separate both absolute-value bars.

The initial e loop and upright t survive above and below the deletion; at the right is a small s turn followed by the separate dot of i. These support the two words et si despite the double crossing lines.
The isolated glyph has one slanting tall stem and a short rightward cross-stroke with an upturned end. There is no separate loop or second upright.
The upper oblique arm of a left-facing inequality is visible, but its lower half is a solid black overdrawn patch. An additional lower bar cannot be excluded or distinguished there.

The first Delta, parenthesized upright 1, equality, and following 1 remain legible through the deletion. Before the final parenthesized A, a small loop and crossed upright could be et or cancellation remnants, so the trailing sequence remains uncertain.
A central vertical stroke projects above and below a loop drawn on both sides of it; a short separate underline lies underneath. The bilateral loop distinguishes Phi from a one-sided b bowl.
The deleted fragment has an upper S-like pair of turns and a heavy descending hooked stroke on the right. No separate i dot can be isolated from the overlapping ink, so Si remains uncertain.
